unloaded-leg-isolation.basis: The moving leg supplies modest local resistance. Repeated 45-second sets can develop basic local strength and endurance; brief single support is incidental.

bilateral-calf-work.basis: Bilateral or split-stance heel raises repeatedly load the plantar flexors. The fixed bodyweight load has a modest strength ceiling and a useful local endurance stimulus.

wall-calf-strength.basis: The wall-supported calf action directly loads the plantar flexors without an unsupported balance challenge. Fixed leverage limits maximal-force progression.

unilateral-calf-strength.basis: One leg bears bodyweight through the calf raise. This offers appreciable local strength and endurance work plus modest unsupported stance control.

tibialis-strength.basis: Wall-leaning toe raises load dorsiflexion directly. This is local force and endurance work; support removes the balance task.

toe-and-heel-walking.basis: Repeated forefoot or heel loading trains basic ankle endurance and controlled shifts of the support base.

hamstring-mobility-flow.basis: The unweighted reach or straight-leg pattern repeatedly approaches posterior-chain range. Its principal contribution is active mobility, with simple movement sequencing.

ordinary-squat.basis: Repeated bilateral or split-stance squatting supplies fixed bodyweight resistance. Forty-five-second sets train local endurance more strongly than high maximal strength.

shallow-squat.basis: The shallow squat or assisted sit-to-stand offers entry-level leg loading and endurance; neither its range nor its fixed resistance establishes advanced strength.

squat-arm-pattern.basis: Bodyweight squatting provides leg strength/endurance work while the arm or trunk action adds a simple coordinated pattern. Range is only credited where deliberately practiced.

squat-calf-pattern.basis: Combining loaded knee bends with heel raises sustains leg work and requires elementary control of a changing support base.

light-squat-calf-pattern.basis: The shallow knee/heel action and arm pattern supply modest sustained local loading and basic interlimb timing.

lunge-and-reach.basis: The lunge or squat transition loads the legs through repeated 45-second sets. Reaching, turning, or raising a knee adds modest stance control and coordination; this is not rapid agility practice.

lateral-lunge.basis: The lateral lunge directly loads the legs while exploring hip/adductor range. Controlled direction changes do not by themselves establish a speed or agility stimulus.

deep-squat-mobility.basis: The deep loaded squat and side shift or thoracic turn combine appreciable local endurance with deliberate end-range hip/ankle/trunk mobility.

squat-locomotion.basis: Travel in the low squat sustains leg loading and trains controlled foot placement. The deliberate pace limits speed and agility claims.

bilateral-leg-hold.basis: A fixed bilateral or split stance holds the knee/hip extensors under sustained load. Forty-five seconds supports local isometric endurance and moderate angle-specific strength.

wall-sit-march.basis: Alternating feet during a wall sit increases unilateral leg loading and sequencing while the wall supplies trunk support.

pistol-strength.basis: A deep unilateral squat or bottom hold loads one leg at demanding leverage and range. It supports advanced task-specific strength, local endurance, mobility, and single-leg control.

partial-single-leg-squat.basis: Unilateral-biased knee extension supplies more local force demand than an ordinary bilateral squat, with a limited rather than specialist progression at the shown depth and support.

sissy-squat.basis: The unsupported knee-dominant lean creates demanding quadriceps leverage. It is local strength/endurance work with deliberate stance control, not ballistic power.

single-leg-hinge.basis: The unsupported single-leg hinge or hip rotation challenges dynamic stance control and posterior-chain endurance. Bodyweight resistance limits the maximal-strength ceiling.

light-single-leg-hinge.basis: The unsupported reach/hinge practices single-leg control with modest posterior-chain loading and coordinated trunk/limb movement.

supported-hip-hinge.basis: The rear foot against the wall reduces the balance task while hip rotation and the hinge practice useful active hip control.

bodyweight-hinge.basis: An unloaded bilateral hinge offers basic posterior-chain loading and active hip range; it does not provide progressive heavy resistance.

wall-hip-isometric.basis: Pressing the thigh into a wall permits sustained self-scaled hip-abductor force. It is local isometric strength/endurance rather than unsupported balance.

local-self-resistance.basis: Deliberate opposing force from the other hand, leg, or wall can meaningfully load the named local action. The estimate assumes active resistance throughout the 45-second block, without inferring a measured maximal load.

supported-light-hold.basis: The supported limb press/hold provides modest angle-specific local loading; support removes a meaningful postural balance requirement.

arm-endurance.basis: Holding or cycling the arms against gravity supplies modest shoulder/arm endurance and entry-level local strength. No external resistance or maximal-speed intent is assumed.

hand-endurance.basis: Opening or spreading the fingers while holding the arms forward supports basic hand control and local endurance, without a substantial maximal-force stimulus.

posing.basis: Voluntary posing sustains local contractions and practices body-position control. Unmeasured co-contraction is not equated with high external resistance.

arm-pressback-hold.basis: The bent-over arm hold sustains the shoulder extensors against gravity. It primarily trains angle-specific local endurance with limited fixed resistance.

tree-and-knee-balance.basis: An unsupported eyes-open single-leg stance practices that static balance task. It offers limited stance endurance, with no implied transfer to perturbation recovery.

dynamic-leg-balance.basis: The unsupported moving-leg pattern changes the center of mass and practices single-leg control, active hip range, and basic limb sequencing.

figure-four-squat-balance.basis: The unsupported figure-four squat adds substantial stance-leg work and hip range to a dynamic single-leg balance task.

dancer-balance.basis: The unsupported dancer hold combines an extended single-leg posture with deliberate shoulder/hip range. Its ceiling is specific to this unperturbed pose.

tandem-balance.basis: Tandem or feet-together stance narrows the support base; stepping or head movement practices modest sensory/postural control without a rapid external perturbation.

single-leg-head-motion.basis: Head motion during unsupported single-leg stance adds a vestibular challenge to a narrow support base.

tiptoe-head-motion.basis: Rising onto the forefeet while moving the head and fixing gaze challenges a reduced support base and eye/head coordination.

gentle-weight-shift.basis: A controlled shift or backward step practices basic foot placement and postural control without sustained substantial loading or rapid direction changes.

gaze-march.basis: Marching while coordinating the eyes and head adds a modest visual/vestibular task to changing single support. It does not supply an unpredictable reaction stimulus.

gaze-isolation.basis: Prescribed eye/finger/head tracking directly practices visual-motor coordination. Predictable tracking is not reaction-time training; ordinary standing is not credited as balance work.

basic-neck-mobility.basis: Controlled unresisted cervical movement practices the demonstrated neck range. It does not establish a significant strength, aerobic, or reaction-time stimulus.

basic-joint-mobility.basis: Controlled unresisted joint movement practices basic available range. Activation, ordinary bracing, and merely moving a limb are not treated as substantial strength or endurance training.

ordinary-static-stretch.basis: The held stretch directly practices the named joint or tissue range for 45 seconds. The rating is local to that range and assumes a controlled end position rather than specialist contortion.

unsupported-standing-stretch.basis: The stretch directly practices local range while requiring basic single-leg or changing-support control. The balance contribution is secondary and limited.

advanced-floor-stretch.basis: The pigeon or hands-on-floor fold practices a comparatively large hip/posterior-chain range. The claim is about that specific position, not universal flexibility.

active-mobility-sequence.basis: The controlled sequence intentionally explores local joint/trunk range with simple sequencing. It is not assigned substantial resistance or cardiorespiratory loading.

isolated-face-control.basis: The deliberate facial action practices elementary local motor control. The unresisted movement is not credited with general coordination, strength, or aerobic capacity.

jaw-mobility.basis: The controlled jaw movement practices available mandibular range. No meaningful external resistance or whole-body capacity stimulus is inferred.

breathing-only.basis: Breathing control, vocalized exhalation, or abdominal drawing-in does not itself establish cardiorespiratory endurance or another substantial stimulus on these ten axes. Zero does not mean the practice has no other purpose.

pelvic-floor-local.basis: The deliberate pelvic-floor squeeze directly practices a local contraction and sustained control. This is basic local strength/endurance, not a whole-body fitness claim.

low-impact-whole-body.basis: Repeated steps or knee raises recruit substantial lower-body muscle mass at a moderate pace. They can develop basic aerobic/local endurance and simple interlimb timing, without high-force or maximal-speed claims.

light-breath-led-squat.basis: Slow shallow knee bends provide mild local loading while arms and breathing follow a predictable pattern. Deliberate breathing alone is not an aerobic stimulus.

gentle-mobility-and-coordination.basis: The gentle arm/trunk/step sequence explores modest range and basic movement timing. The shown movement does not justify substantial resistance, ballistic force, or vigorous aerobic claims.

breathing-arm-endurance.basis: The raised or closing arms supply mild local endurance work and basic breath/movement timing. The prescribed exhalation does not imply aerobic conditioning.

abdominal-drawing-in.basis: Repeated abdominal drawing-in practices low-load local trunk control and endurance, without a measurable heavy-resistance or cardiorespiratory stimulus.

marching-technique-supported.basis: Supported or seated knee lifting supplies modest hip-flexor loading and rhythmic limb practice. Support removes an important balance challenge and the pace is not sprinting.

marching-on-one-leg.basis: Repeated knee drive on one stance leg combines local endurance with an unsupported changing-center-of-mass task and elementary running-pattern timing.

kick-mobility.basis: The large unweighted leg arc practices active hip range and controlled single-leg support. A large arc is not automatically a maximal-power strike.

technical-kick.basis: A deliberate martial kick coordinates trunk and limb acceleration over single-leg support. Unloaded striking supports modest limb speed and power, not heavy maximal-force training.

single-technical-strike.basis: The rehearsed strike/block practices timed arm/trunk action and modest unloaded acceleration. A known loop supplies no reaction stimulus unless the runtime adds an external cue.

boxing-combination.basis: The linked boxing/striking sequence coordinates multiple arm, trunk, and sometimes foot actions. Repeated 45-second work can train basic aerobic endurance and competent task-specific sequencing with modest unloaded limb speed.

boxing-evasion.basis: The rehearsed slip, roll, duck, or pullback practices accurate body repositioning and basic movement timing. There is no unpredictable opponent response in the demonstration.

slow-core-pattern.basis: Controlled trunk bending or rotation with limb motion supplies basic local endurance and intersegment timing. An unloaded chop is not assumed to be an explosive throw.

dance-and-steps.basis: The repeated learned step pattern coordinates changing foot placements and arm/trunk rhythm. It supports modest aerobic conditioning, planned repositioning, and task-specific coordination.

capoeira-evasion.basis: The low lateral evasion sustains leg loading while coordinating trunk position and a deliberate weight shift.

ballet-grand-plie.basis: The deep turned-out knee bend loads the legs while deliberately exploring hip/ankle range and controlled alignment.

yoga-loaded-standing-hold.basis: The wide stance sustains local leg work while holding the arms and trunk in a specific position. It offers basic posture control and useful local hip/trunk range.

leg-resistance-with-arm-pattern.basis: Repeated loaded leg or trunk action supplies sustained local work and elementary multi-segment timing. Forceful naming or exhalation does not establish ballistic power.

light-lateral-lunge-reach.basis: The shallow lateral lunge and reach give mild leg loading, active adductor/trunk range, and a simple coordinated weight shift.

coordination-finger-switch.basis: Switching the thumb and little finger deliberately practices a nontrivial independent hand pattern. It makes a local dexterity claim, not a whole-body coordination claim.

coordination-tutting.basis: The geometric hand/arm sequence deliberately practices precise independent segment positions and transitions. This is a comparatively advanced task-specific coordination pattern.

coordination-arm-wave.basis: Passing a wave across both arms requires serial joint isolation and controlled timing; the stimulus is coordination rather than heavy resistance.

coordination-teacup.basis: The continuous teacup path combines shoulder, elbow, wrist, and trunk orientation with constrained hand position. It practices local mobility and a complex learned sequence.

coordination-clap-and-knee.basis: Alternating overhead and under-leg claps with knee raises practices a linked arm/leg sequence and modest rhythmic whole-body endurance.

basic-wall-pushing.basis: The inclined wall/raised-support push supplies low-to-moderate local resistance and useful pushing endurance. Stable support and the fixed incline limit maximal-strength claims.

fingertip-wall-pushing.basis: The fingertip wall push-up deliberately loads finger support and pushing muscles. Its local strength claim is limited by the supported incline.

rear-foot-wall-split-squat.basis: The wall positions the rear foot while the front leg performs substantial unilateral work. The exercise develops leg strength/endurance and modest stance control.

lateral-skip.basis: Traveling lateral skips coordinate repeated takeoffs and landings with planned lateral foot placement.

crossover-locomotion.basis: Crossing steps while traveling requires linked lateral footwork, planned repositioning, and relatively complex interlimb timing.

basic-jacks.basis: Repeated two-foot jacks provide rhythmic whole-body work and a simple synchronized arm/leg pattern. Small habitual bounces offer only entry-level elastic power and cadence practice.

complex-jacks.basis: Crossing or adding strikes/arm circles to jacks increases arm/leg sequencing while retaining moderate repeated aerobic and local endurance work.

squat-jacks.basis: Repeated jumping knee bends combine substantial leg endurance with vigorous whole-body work and moderate repeated lower-body power.

running-in-place.basis: Rapid alternating steps recruit substantial muscle mass for the full block and practice limb-cycle speed. Running in place is not assigned maximal overground sprint ability.

basic-pogo.basis: Repeated short elastic hops load the ankle plantar flexors and practice basic takeoff/landing rhythm. The small displacement limits the high-force power claim.

mixed-jump-rope-pattern.basis: Changing the feet or coordinating a clap/strike with repeated hops adds task-specific timing to rhythmic whole-body and elastic lower-leg work.

pogo-gaze-pattern.basis: Repeated bounces combined with head movement and fixed gaze add eye/head timing and modest landing control to elastic leg endurance work.

bilateral-power-jump.basis: Deliberate substantial takeoffs and controlled landings train rapid lower-body force and local leg endurance. The repeated 45-second format limits maximal-quality power practice.

jump-and-strike.basis: Combining substantial jumps with arm strikes trains repeated leg power and interlimb timing with vigorous whole-body work.

jumping-lunges.basis: Rapid split-stance takeoffs and alternating landings produce vigorous aerobic/local endurance work, substantial leg power, and controlled stance switching.

rotating-two-leg-jump.basis: A deliberate airborne turn requires rapid accurate whole-body repositioning and landing control alongside lower-body power and endurance.

small-lateral-hops.basis: Repeated small lateral hops or twists practice quick planned repositioning and elastic leg work. Small amplitude limits maximal-force power and balance claims.

lateral-power-bound.basis: The forceful lateral takeoff and controlled landing train lateral power, planned repositioning, and dynamic postural control.

single-leg-rotational-jump.basis: An unsupported unilateral takeoff with an airborne turn and controlled landing combines advanced local power with dynamic single-leg and spatial control.

single-leg-power-jump.basis: A deliberate one-leg vertical takeoff and stick landing provide advanced task-specific unilateral power and substantial dynamic stance control.

single-leg-repeated-hop.basis: Repeated unsupported one-leg hops sustain local leg work and elastic power while practicing repeated single-leg landing control.

pivot-and-gaze.basis: Turning while maintaining or resetting a visual target practices planned spatial repositioning, modest stance control, and head/eye sequencing.

power-skipping.basis: Traveling bounds or forceful skips deliberately emphasize lower-body impulse and coordinated unilateral takeoff/landing. Repeated blocks also provide substantial whole-body work.

sprinting.basis: Actual overground sprinting directly practices high running speed and rapid lower-body force. Repeated 45-second efforts give strong aerobic conditioning potential but do not establish an elite speed or VO2 ceiling.

backward-running.basis: Backward running trains rhythmic whole-body endurance and competent task-specific locomotor timing/speed with modest spatial control.

floor-local-endurance.basis: The supported floor action repeatedly loads the named local muscle group against gravity or a short bodyweight lever. It supplies basic local strength/endurance without high whole-body aerobic demand.

floor-static-support.basis: The sustained plank or bridge supports bodyweight through a stable base. Its primary contribution is local isometric endurance and moderate task-specific strength, not standing balance.

floor-cross-limb-control.basis: Controlled limb paths over a stable floor-supported trunk develop local endurance and elementary independent limb timing. A stable support base does not justify a general balance rating.

floor-dynamic-support.basis: Changing limb support while maintaining a loaded trunk gives substantial local endurance, moderate bodyweight strength, and coordinated segment control. It is not treated as unsupported standing balance.

hard-floor-hold.basis: The long lever or low loaded position sustains substantial local force for the block. This is demanding isometric endurance with moderate task-specific maximal-force potential.

one-arm-plank.basis: Unilateral upper-body support creates a demanding fixed lever and anti-rotation task. It supports substantial local strength/endurance and modest multi-segment control.

standard-floor-push.basis: Repeated pushing through a fixed bodyweight lever gives substantial local strength and endurance. Hand spacing or knuckle contact alone is not treated as a specialist strength progression.

advanced-floor-push.basis: The asymmetric, inclined, or low traveling pushing lever increases local force demand beyond a standard push-up. The fixed demonstrated variation supports substantial task-specific strength and endurance.

easier-floor-push.basis: Knee support or a short assisted pushing lever offers basic local pushing strength and endurance, without the load of a full or asymmetric push-up.

explosive-floor-push.basis: A deliberate ballistic push that leaves the floor directly trains rapid upper-body force. Repeated 45-second execution adds local endurance while limiting fresh maximal-power repetitions.

knee-burpee.basis: Repeated standing-to-floor transitions with an easier push-up recruit substantial muscle mass. They support vigorous aerobic/local endurance and basic sequencing; no unshown maximal jump is assumed.

burpee-plank-jacks.basis: Repeated full-body floor-to-standing transitions and plank jacks sustain vigorous whole-body and local endurance demands, with moderate pushing strength and basic sequencing.

plank-hops.basis: Rapid hopping while supporting the trunk trains vigorous repeated local/aerobic work and coordinated foot placement. It offers modest lower-limb impulse rather than maximal jumping power.

mountain-climbers.basis: Repeated knee drives from a plank combine rhythmic whole-body work with local trunk/shoulder endurance and simple leg-cycle timing.

mountain-climber-push-up.basis: Combining full push-ups and rapid knee drives produces substantial pushing/trunk endurance with vigorous whole-body work and linked limb sequencing.

floor-light-support-motion.basis: The moving limbs add local endurance and simple segment timing to floor support. The slow controlled action is not assigned a substantial aerobic or speed ceiling.

posterior-chain-hard-lever.basis: The demanding knee/hip lever or unilateral support directly loads the posterior chain/adductors. It supplies substantial local strength and endurance without implying a universal strength level.

opposed-floor-isometric.basis: Pressing the thigh or knee against the hands supplies self-scaled local opposing force and endurance; no measured maximal loading is inferred.

floor-rolling-coordination.basis: The roll, sit-through, or changing-support transition practices linked trunk/limb timing and some local endurance. Floor contact supplies a stable support context.

long-lever-walkout.basis: Walking the hands into a long lever increases trunk/shoulder force and local endurance while controlling a predictable changing support pattern.

mobility-loaded-floor.basis: The three-legged downward-dog position combines local shoulder/leg endurance with deliberate posterior-chain range and basic limb control.

bicycle-crunch.basis: Alternating opposite elbow/knee motion loads the trunk while practicing a clear cross-body sequence. The supported posture is not a balance or high-aerobic task.

v-up-strength.basis: Raising straight legs and trunk together creates demanding abdominal/hip-flexor leverage and moderate coordination.

pilates-hundred.basis: Sustained trunk/leg positioning with repeated arm pulses produces demanding local endurance. The prescribed breathing pattern is not treated as independent aerobic conditioning.

crawl-conditioning.basis: Traveling on multiple supports recruits substantial muscle mass while practicing predictable contralateral foot/hand placement. This supports moderate aerobic and local endurance plus task-specific coordination.

low-loaded-crawl.basis: The low traveling support keeps the limbs and trunk under substantial load while coordinating advancing contacts.

large-floor-mobility.basis: The supported frog position directly practices comparatively large hip-abduction range. The score is specific to that joint position.

unilateral-incline-scapula.basis: The unilateral or elevated pike support increases direct scapular loading while maintaining a supported base. It supplies moderate local strength and endurance.

step-calf-raise.basis: The step permits loaded calf work over a larger ankle range. The direct stimulus remains local strength/endurance, with a modest active-range contribution.

burpee-broad-jump.basis: Full-body transitions followed by deliberate horizontal takeoffs combine vigorous whole-body/local endurance with substantial repeated lower-body power and sequencing.

hamstring-mobility-flow-stop-go.basis: The unweighted reach or straight-leg pattern repeatedly approaches posterior-chain range. Its principal contribution is active mobility, with simple movement sequencing. The existing unpredictable visual stop/go cue adds basic response practice; its frequency is not a measured reaction-time ceiling.

low-impact-whole-body-stop-go.basis: Repeated steps or knee raises recruit substantial lower-body muscle mass at a moderate pace. They can develop basic aerobic/local endurance and simple interlimb timing, without high-force or maximal-speed claims. The existing unpredictable visual stop/go cue adds basic response practice; its frequency is not a measured reaction-time ceiling.

gentle-mobility-and-coordination-stop-go.basis: The gentle arm/trunk/step sequence explores modest range and basic movement timing. The shown movement does not justify substantial resistance, ballistic force, or vigorous aerobic claims. The existing unpredictable visual stop/go cue adds basic response practice; its frequency is not a measured reaction-time ceiling.

single-technical-strike-stop-go.basis: The rehearsed strike/block practices timed arm/trunk action and modest unloaded acceleration. A known loop supplies no reaction stimulus unless the runtime adds an external cue. The existing unpredictable visual stop/go cue adds basic response practice; its frequency is not a measured reaction-time ceiling.

boxing-combination-stop-go.basis: The linked boxing/striking sequence coordinates multiple arm, trunk, and sometimes foot actions. Repeated 45-second work can train basic aerobic endurance and competent task-specific sequencing with modest unloaded limb speed. The existing unpredictable visual stop/go cue adds basic response practice; its frequency is not a measured reaction-time ceiling.

boxing-step-pattern-stop-go.basis: The side step and knee drive add sustained whole-body movement to rehearsed punches. Timing is practiced, but controlled foot placement does not imply high agility. The existing unpredictable visual stop/go cue adds basic response practice; its frequency is not a measured reaction-time ceiling.

dance-and-steps-stop-go.basis: The repeated learned step pattern coordinates changing foot placements and arm/trunk rhythm. It supports modest aerobic conditioning, planned repositioning, and task-specific coordination. The existing unpredictable visual stop/go cue adds basic response practice; its frequency is not a measured reaction-time ceiling.

side-shuffle-stop-go.basis: Repeated lateral shuffles practice planned quick foot placement and direction changes. The shown pace supports moderate aerobic demand and limited foot speed. The existing unpredictable visual stop/go cue adds basic response practice; its frequency is not a measured reaction-time ceiling.
